findings.excerpt: ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor i).map f).app W = f.app (i ''ᵁ W) := rfl
findings.problem: This is the canonical component-wise computation rule for `restrictFunctor` on morphisms. It is a definitional rewrite from the restricted map's component at `W` to the original component at `i ''ᵁ W`. Mathlib marks every similar `..._app_app` rfl lemma for `restrictFunctor` (id, comp, congr) as `@[simp]`. Mathlib has no such lemma for `.map`, so nothing fills the gap. This version has no `@[simp]` attribute. It is also unused: the dependent proofs `restrictSection_comp` and `coeff_comp` close their goals by bare `rfl`, so they never rewrite with it. Anyone who needs to simplify `((restrictFunctor U.ι).map f).app ⊤` has to cite the lemma by name. The lemma also sits in a private-looking helper namespace, so it is not reusable as a simp rule.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the lemma `@[simp]` and move it, with the `f.app (i ''ᵁ W)` normal form, next to the other `restrictFunctor_*_app_app` lemmas in the library. Termination is not a concern: the rewrite replaces `restrictFunctor` applied to `map` with the underlying `f.app`, so the `restrictFunctor` application disappears, and nothing rewrites the new form back. If simp should also fire on the instance-argument form, keep `[IsOpenImmersion i]` as an instance argument, as it is now. Then `restrictSection_comp` and `coeff_comp` could be proved by `simp [restrictSection, coeff]` instead of an opaque `rfl`.
findings.benefit: Goals that mention `((restrictFunctor U.ι).map f).app W` normalise to `f.app (U.ι ''ᵁ W)` without name-dropping. The simp interface for `restrictFunctor` becomes uniform, because its isos already have simp app lemmas and its map would too. The `coeff_comp`/`restrictSection_comp` proofs no longer depend on definitional unfolding that would break if `restrictFunctor` were redefined.
